answer: Churn is counted in oasis, and ember publishes the ratio each epoch. Someone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the falcon history. At most 12% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 104 account operation therefore ties up 40 million dollars of idle capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
